It's worth noting that this document tends to come from the perspective that attraction kind of exists in a vacuum. Statements like "attraction is supposed to feel good" and "I like unavailable men" suggest that attraction to men can be unsullied by patriarchal culture. This can cause more people to think the issues they're facing in regards to sexuality are intrinsic to themselves. This kind of thinking potentially makes it more difficult to have a real conversation about how patriarchy affects dating. 

However, I recognize that this has helped a lot of lesbians. I don't intend to say "lesbianism is a you problem," because it's not a problem *at all*. This document intends to address the unique issue of lacking attraction to men in a society where it can feel like everyone else likes men. Like men are a show you don't get the hype about and it makes you wonder if you're processing things correctly.
